answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any disruption to supply continuity carries outsized risk right now. Memory c1 indicates incumbent renewal has historically preserved integration stability and on-time delivery across cycles, which directly protects against the current no-buffer exposure. Memory c2 shows switching to a low-cost vendor can cut unit cost and onboard quickly, but that record doesn't establish onboarding speed under a 14-day deadline with no production slack — the conditions differ materially from today's, so I want the original c2 record verified before trusting it as precedent for switching now. Negotiate_terms (c4) is foreclosed this cycle since the incumbent has already refused to reopen price. Given only one sourcing decision is available, I'm leaning toward a short, guarded renewal (not a multi-year lock-in like c6) to preserve continuity through the immediate risk window, while explicitly not resolving the 18% cost mandate this cycle — that gap must be flagged rather than papered over, since finance's target is unmet and a vendor switch or renegotiation will need to be revisited next review with more lead time. Adding a second source (c3) addresses a different risk (component shortage) and doesn't relieve the imminent contract expiry, so it's not the right single move this cycle either.
